subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A rectangle has area 48 cm^2 and width 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explain: Length = 48 / 6 = 8 cm, so perimeter = 2 x (8 + 6) = 28 cm.

questions.q: In a right-angled triangle, which ratio equals the opposite divided by the hypotenuse?
A right-angled triangle has the two shorter sides 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the hypotenuse?
An exterior angle of a regular polygon is 40°. How many sides does it have?
An equilateral triangle has all sides equal. What is the size of each interior angle?
questions.explain: Angles sum to 180 deg and all three are equal, so each is 180 / 3 = 60 deg.

questions.q: The angle in a semicircle (in the triangle on a diameter) is always:
questions.explain: By the circle theorem, the angle in a semicircle is a right angle, 90 deg.

questions.q: Two angles lie on a straight line. One is 110°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°, so 180° − 110° = 70°.

A line drawn from the centre of a circle to a point on the circumference is called the:
questions.explain: A radius joins the centre to the circumference.

questions.q: A quarter circle has radius 8 cm. What is its arc length? (Use pi = 3.14)
questions.explain: Full circumference = pi x 16 = 50.24 cm, and a quarter is 50.24 / 4 = 12.56 cm.

questions.q: A cylinder has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm. What is its volume? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
What is the exact value of tan 0°?
questions.explain: tan 0° = 0 since the opposite side is 0.

questions.q: A circle has diameter 10 cm. What is its area? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
questions.explain: Radius = 5 cm, so area = π × 5^2 = π × 25 ≈ 78.5 cm^2.

Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90°, 100° and 80°. What is the fourth angle?
questions.explain: Angles in a quadrilateral sum to 360°, so 360° − 90° − 100° − 80° = 90°.
